items.answer: 8 and 9

items.stem: A student claims: "In a right-angled triangle with legs 3 and 4, c² = 3 + 4 = 7." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Square each side first: c² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5.
items.markingKey: Square each side first: c² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points.
items.answer: Coordinates are ordered: the first number is the horizontal position and the second the vertical, so (2, 5) is 2 across and 5 up, but (5, 2) is 5 across and 2 up.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Coordinates are ordered: the first number is the horizontal position and the second the vertical, so (2, 5) is 2 across and 5 up, but (5, 2) is 5 across and 2 up. items.answer: Divide each term by 3: 6y + 9 = 3(2y + 3).
items.markingKey: Divide each term by 3: 6y + 9 = 3(2y + 3). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Investigate rotating the point A(6, 5) repeatedly by 90° clockwise about the origin. (a) Find the images A₁, A₂, A₃ and A₄. (b) Describe the shape formed by A, A₁, A₂, A₃. (c) Explain why A₄ = A.
items.answer: (a) (5, −6), (−6, −5), (−5, 6), (6, 5) (b) a square centred on the origin (c) four quarter turns make a full turn of 360°
items.markingKey: (a) (5, −6), (−6, −5), (−5, 6), (6, 5) (b) a square centred on the origin (c) four quarter turns make a full turn of 360°. Rotation rules applied (M1 A1 A1); pattern / symmetry identified (B: R1); clear notation (C1).

items.stem: Distinguish between a sample and a population.
items.answer: A population is the whole group of interest; a sample is a smaller part of it used to draw conclusions about the whole.
items.markingKey: A population is the whole group of interest; a sample is a smaller part of it used to draw conclusions about the whole. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain how to construct an angle of 120° using only a ruler and compasses.

items.stem: A roof in Dubai has a horizontal area of 142 m². During a storm 17 mm of rain falls. (a) Convert 17 mm to metres. (b) Find the volume of water that falls on the roof in m³. (c) How many litres is that? (d) How many 200-litre barrels would it fill?

items.markingKey: Multiply the numbers and add the exponents (M1); adjust so 1 ≤ a < 10 (M1); 3.51 × 10¹ (A1).

items.stem: Omar and Lukas play a game with two fair six-sided dice. Omar wins if the difference between the scores is 0, 1 or 2; otherwise Lukas wins. (a) Draw a sample space diagram of the differences. (b) Find P(Omar wins). (c) Is the game fair? If not, suggest a change to make it fair.

items.markingKey: (a) a 6 × 6 grid of differences (b) 24/36 = 2/3 (c) not fair; e.g. Omar wins only on a difference of 1 or 2 (10 + 8 = 18 outcomes, 18/36 = 1/2), which is fair. Systematic sample space (M1 A1); probability (A1); fairness/change justified (R1 C1).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "congruent"?
options: Exactly the same shape and size; one can be mapped onto the other by translations, rotations and reflections
A transformation that flips a shape over a mirror line; each point and its image are the same distance from the line
Turning in the same direction as the hands of a clock
The fixed point that does not move during a rotation
items.answer: Exactly the same shape and size; one can be mapped onto the other by translations, rotations and reflections
items.markingKey: A. "congruent" is exactly the same shape and size; one can be mapped onto the other by translations, rotations and reflections.

items.stem: Food stored for an expedition lasts 3 climbers for 9 days. How long would it last 9 climbers?
items.answer: 3 days

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "regular polygon"?
options: Angles on opposite sides of a transversal, between two parallel lines; they are equal (Z-shape)
A triangle with two equal sides and two equal base angles
A polygon with all sides equal and all interior angles equal
The angle between one side and the extension of the next side; the exterior angles of any convex polygon add to 360°
items.answer: A polygon with all sides equal and all interior angles equal
items.markingKey: C. "regular polygon" is a polygon with all sides equal and all interior angles equal.

items.stem: Explain why all triangles with base 15 cm whose top vertex lies on a line parallel to the base, 10 cm above it, have the same area.
items.answer: They all have the same base 15 cm and the same perpendicular height 10 cm, so each area is ½ × 15 × 10 = 75 cm².
items.markingKey: Same base and perpendicular height (R1); area value (A1).

items.stem: Classify each of the following as qualitative, quantitative discrete or quantitative continuous: (a) dress size, (b) the mass of a newborn baby, (c) the number of pets each student owns.
items.answer: (a) quantitative, discrete; (b) quantitative, continuous; (c) quantitative, discrete

items.stem: Ana has two cylinders: A has radius 5 cm and height 20 cm; B has radius 10 cm and height 10 cm. Explain which holds more, and how many times as much.

items.stem: A student claims: "Vertically opposite angles add up to 180°." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.

items.stem: A lift in a Dubai office block has a safe load of 554 kg. A worker of mass 67 kg is moving boxes of 15 kg each.
